investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending, preventing VM assignment and blocking the eval from collecting any required evidence. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration failure localized to the remote-agents scheduling tier, not an eval infrastructure defect.

If those rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range exhaustion at the namespace or org level preventing new kata peer-pod VMs from being allocated even if node-level slots appear available.

Quaternary — a recent cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity without a corresponding workload reduction.

investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot served at eval time was 710 minutes old (evidence: failed-check.evidence, failed-check.message), meaning the workflow either did not trigger, was queued and did not complete, or failed silently without updating the published artifact. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending, preventing VM assignment and blocking the eval from collecting any required evidence. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration failure localized to the remote-agents scheduling tier, not an eval infrastructure defect.

If those rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range exhaustion at the namespace or org level preventing new kata peer-pod VMs from being allocated even if node-level slots appear available.

Quaternary — a recent cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity without a corresponding workload reduction.
